issues.description: The template StockIngredient class defines a getter named retrieveQuantity(), but the template Stock class calls getQuantity() (e.g., in add() and take()). This method-name/signature mismatch causes compilation errors and prevents students from using the provided Stock methods as intended. The problem statement also asks students to add getters for all private fields (implying a getQuantity() method), and the solution uses getQuantity(), so the template's retrieveQuantity() is inconsistent with both the specification and the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template StockIngredient.retrieveQuantity() method to getQuantity() (and keep its return type and behavior), so it matches the calls in Stock and aligns with the problem statement and solution. Alternatively, update Stock.add/take to call retrieveQuantity(), but the preferred fix is to expose a standard getter getQuantity() to conform to the specification.

issues.description: The template defines the quantity accessor as retrieveQuantity() (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java) while the Stock class and the solution use/get expect getQuantity(). The problem statement also instructs to add getters for private fields. This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual getter (quantity) creates confusion and a mismatch between the problem text, the template code students start with, and the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template's retrieveQuantity() method to getQuantity(), or add a getQuantity() method that delegates to retrieveQuantity(), so that the Stock class, the problem statement expectation (getters), and the solution align on the same getter name.
